sections.h2: Who values your house and who bills you
sections.html:
Think of the system as a relay. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets each parcel's assessed value. Around October 1 the sheriff sends out and collects the bill. When April 15 passes with money still owed, the county clerk is handed the baton.

The sheriff doesn't decide what your house is worth. Your bill multiplies the PVA's figure by the rate of every taxing body over the parcel: the state, the county, a school district and any special district. If your house is inside Winchester, which is both the seat and the only city, ask the city whether it bills a separate city tax and when.

sections.h2: Where to pay a Clark County bill
sections.html:
The sheriff's office is in the basement of the Governor James Clark Judicial Building in Winchester, and the number for questions is (859) 744-4390. Payment is accepted several ways.

Ways to pay the Clark County sheriff
MethodWhat to know
By mailCheck or money order to 17 Cleveland Avenue, Winchester, KY 40391; the USPS postmark counts, private meters do not
Drop boxCheck or money order in the box off West Broadway, with the bill number, map number or address written on it
OnlineDebit, credit or Google Pay through the sheriff's website, with merchant fees
In personCheck, money order or cash; cards with fees; weekday hours of 8:00 am to 4:00 pm
Bank counterA downtown bank branch on West Broadway takes checks and money orders for the exact amount, with the bill, and no cash

No bill by October 15? Call the sheriff. If a buyer or a mortgage company is supposed to pay, forward the bill to them right away.

KRS 134.015 fixes these dates, and they repeat annually.

  • Through November 1: pay in full and take a 2 percent discount.
  • November 2 to December 31: the bill as printed.
  • Every day in January: 5 percent is added.
  • February 1 to April 15: a 10 percent penalty plus a 10 percent add-on.

At the close of business on April 15 the county clerk takes whatever is still unpaid. Payments made at the clerk's office carry a 20 percent county attorney fee, a 10 percent clerk fee and monthly interest of 1 percent, and delinquent bills can be sold to a third party. Bills go out October 1, the face amount holds until December 31, and collection passes to the clerk after April 15.

sections.h2: What to know about Clark County property
sections.html:
Clark County sits next to Lexington and belongs to its metropolitan area. It covers 255 square miles. In 2020 it had 36,972 residents, 14,917 households and 16,116 housing units. About 65.6 percent of occupied homes were owned and 34.4 percent rented, with 7.4 percent of units vacant. Around 71 percent of residents live in urban parts of the county, and the rest live where acreage and farm parcels change hands.

The Kentucky River, Red River, Lulbegrud Creek and Boone's Creek cross the county, so a parcel near the water deserves a look at flood risk before you list. Manufacturing around Winchester, helped by I-64 and the Mountain Parkway, supports the in-town market.

sections.h2: How to challenge an assessed value
sections.html:
Call the Clark County PVA at (859) 745-0250 and request a conference before the roll's public review closes. The review runs thirteen days from the first Monday of May, and no appeal can start without the conference. A phone call counts.

Not satisfied? File a written petition with the clerk by the first workday after review ends. Name the parcel, give your reasons and state what you believe is fair cash value. The hearing follows about a month later, and the board wants facts: sale listings, construction costs, loan papers.

Officials can start a review too. The county judge/executive, a mayor or a school superintendent may ask the board in writing to look at specific parcels, which is how some values rise without the owner filing anything. The plan: confer, file, bring comparable sales and pay on the figure you claim.

An owner who has reached 65, or who is totally disabled, can have a set sum removed from the home's assessed value. The state figure is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and a fresh amount is published every second year.

File with the Clark County PVA. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport shows age. Disability claims require a federal or retirement system classification, and most renew yearly.

Title companies pay the balance at the closing table out of your price. Ask the sheriff what the current bill stands at, and ask the clerk whether an earlier bill turned into a certificate of delinquency. Under KRS 134.015 the lien from an unpaid year stays with the land for eleven years whoever owns it, so a buyer's title search will turn it up.

The cheapest time to clear a balance is before April 15, while the sheriff still has the bill and the extra cost is limited to the penalty and add-on. Afterward the clerk's percentages stack up, and an outside investor can buy the claim. An empty, inherited or run-down house can still sell to an investor who accepts it unrepaired and pays the tax out of the price. Ask for that payoff to be shown as its own line on the settlement statement.

At closing, ask the agent to divide the current year by the date the deed transfers, so each side covers its own months.

A person who buys after the bill is issued may still receive it in the old owner's name, because value is set each year at an earlier date. Forward any mail you get after closing to the new owner or their lender.

Start with the PVA record. Ask whether the acreage, building details and any outbuildings match what stands on the land, since errors flow straight into the bill. Then confirm the exemption on file still fits the owner. If the PVA has your property as the wrong size, a buyer will see the problem in the assessment history.

Next, collect your payment proof for the year. The sheriff can confirm what has been paid, and a bank or servicer that pays from escrow should show the same. Keep receipts together with your deed so the closing agent has everything in one place.

Last, think about timing. A sale in the autumn means the bill may just have gone out, while a sale after February 1 means penalties may already be running. If you're up against a deadline, an as-is cash purchase that pays the tax from the proceeds can close faster than a financed one, and it needs no repairs or showings. Whichever way you go, get the payoff in writing before you agree to a price.

faqs.q: Which Clark County phone numbers cover tax bills and values?
faqs.a: Call the sheriff's office at (859) 744-4390 for bill and payment questions. For value questions call the Clark County PVA at (859) 745-0250.

faqs.q: When do Clark County bills get mailed?
faqs.a: Around October 1 each year, and they also appear online. Owners without a printed bill by October 15 should call the sheriff.

faqs.q: Does the Clark County sheriff accept cash?
faqs.a: Yes, at the sheriff's office counter in Winchester. The downtown bank location does not accept cash.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my Clark County home for tax?
faqs.a: The Clark County PVA, not the sheriff. The sheriff only collects the bill that results from the PVA's assessment and the local tax rates.

faqs.q: What if I miss the April 15 date in Clark County?
faqs.a: The unpaid bill transfers to the county clerk. There a 20 percent county attorney fee, a 10 percent clerk fee and 1 percent interest per month apply, and the bill can be sold to a third party.
